title: Benjamin Franklin: We Must Hang Together!
culture_region: India / Greece / USA / South Africa / World
summary: Signing a document that made them traitors under British law punishable by hanging, Franklin famously quipped: 'We must indeed all hang together, or most assuredly we shall all hang separately!'
keywords: Benjamin Franklin: We Must Hang Together!
full_text:
July 4, 1776. The Pennsylvania State House in Philadelphia.

Fifty-six delegates of the Second Continental Congress were gathered to sign the Declaration of Independence.

Every man in that room knew the immense peril of their act: by appending their signatures, they were committing high treason against King George III! If the revolution failed, British soldiers would arrest every signer and execute them on the gallows.

A somber, tense atmosphere gripped the assembly.

John Hancock, President of Congress, boldly scrawled his famous oversized signature and declared gravely:
"Gentlemen, there must be no pulling different ways; we must all hang together!"

Seventy-year-old Benjamin Franklin—famed inventor, diplomat, and philosopher—stepped forward to sign. He turned toward the anxious delegates with a merry twinkle behind his spectacles and delivered one of the greatest puns in history:

**"Yes, Mr. President! We must, indeed, all hang together...
Or most assuredly, we shall all hang separately!"**

The room burst into relieved laughter, breaking the suffocating tension.

In that single witty stroke, Franklin crystallized their existential reality: solidarity was their only shield against the British hangman's noose. Unity in purpose transformed fifty-six vulnerable men into the founding fathers of a free nation.
moral: Solidarity is the indispensable armor of collective freedom; divided we perish, united we prevail.
